chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said:
"When the person in ihram covers his face, he should feed a poor person."
He said, "And there is no harm if the person in ihram sleeps on his face on his mount."

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (consecration for pilgrimage)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for covering the face while in ihram, and is sleeping on the face permitted?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between minor and major prohibitions in Ihram by specifying that covering the face incurs a light fidya of feeding one poor person, while sleeping on the face while mounted is permissible without penalty. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between actions that break the sanctity of the state versus those that are merely disliked or require minor compensation, reflecting the practical ease granted to pilgrims during travel.
